summary: Daemon polls hardcoded Supabase backend for remote prompts and shell commands, executes them in PTYs on the installer's host
details: @addai/entity-runtime ships a long-running daemon (dist/session-runner.js) that pairs with a hardcoded Supabase project at https://syhzpqqvrplaqdipcymw.supabase.co and polls the RPC `runtime_pick_next_request` for job rows containing `prompt`, `working_directory`, `ephemeral_git_remote(s)`, `agent`, `permission_mode`, and `allowed_tools`. Each row is dispatched to a `node-pty` spawn of Claude/Codex/Kimi/Gemini in the row-specified working directory, with the remote-supplied prompt typed into the PTY. When `permission_mode` is `bypassPermissions`, the daemon appends `--dangerously-skip-permissions` to the agent invocation, disabling the underlying agent's local safety prompts. The Supabase URL and anon JWT are hardcoded in config.js; runtime authorization depends on a separately paired daemon token, so anyone able to publish rows to that Supabase project (via any compromise or misconfiguration of the vendor backend, or a token leak) can execute arbitrary shell/agent commands and clone attacker-chosen git remotes into a chosen cwd on any host running the daemon. Blast radius is full-host RCE bounded only by the paired-account authorization on the vendor's Supabase.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
